speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I need to understand your specific skin concerns to proceed. Please describe the lesion you are worried about, including when it first appeared and how it has changed over time.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient reports a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penile shaft and a similar one on the left middle finger, with a significant history of smoking and failed prior treatments. Given the chronic nature and location of these lesions, have you noticed any bleeding, pain, or change in the size or shape of these spots?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The presence of non-healing, crusty, painless lesions in a heavy smoker with a history of failed syphilis and eczema treatment in two distinct sites (penis and finger) is highly suspicious for cutaneous malignancy. I will request a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy_Penile_and_Digital; REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical_Photos_Lesions
